plan.purpose: For the person who just asked for a trip and now wants to see how it goes, day by day, and whether it fits the money: a calm travel notebook to read top to bottom and come back to.
plan.title: Your trip, day by day
plan.composition: The page uses the full width and opens on a ResultHeader. Its h1 is the trip's own name, with the overview as the muted line under it, and the host's actions sit at its right. Below it, a Split at 2:1 makes up the body. The wide left column is the itinerary, one day after another like pages in a travel notebook. Each day has a weekday eyebrow in the accent colour, a short title, then its morning, midday, afternoon and evening as quiet labelled lines. A line hides itself when that part of the day is empty, so arrival and departure days stay short. The narrow right column is the money rail, and it comes first on a narrow screen. It opens with the estimated total as one large figure, then the cost split by category, then the practical notes as a short list. Nothing is boxed except the ProportionBar's own panel. The page uses two heading levels: the h1 in the header and h2 Section titles. Day titles are h3 inside the itinerary Section.

regions.purpose: Names the trip from the result itself and gives the gist of it in a few sentences. The host's download and share actions sit at its right.
elements: ResultHeader: eyebrow "Your trip plan"; title read with $state /result/title (the page's h1); muted line read with $state /result/overview

regions.purpose: The body: the itinerary in the wide left column, with the budget and notes in a narrow rail beside it.
elements: Split ratio "2:1": first child is the Day by day Section (left), second child is a vertical Stack holding the Budget and Good to know Sections (right)

regions.title: Day by day
regions.purpose: The heart of the result: each day of the trip in order, written for reading, not scanning a table.
elements: Section with small number "01", title "Day by day"
Vertical Stack repeated over /result/days, one entry per day, with a Separator between entries:
DateText value $item day, format "weekday", tone accent (the eyebrow)

regions.title: Budget
regions.purpose: Answers the second question at a glance: how much the trip costs and where the money goes. It sits at the top of the rail, next to the first days.
elements: Horizontal Stack: Icon "wallet" beside Metric label "Estimated total", value $state /result/estimated_total, unit read with $state /result/currency, format integer
ProportionBar label "By category", items $state /result/costs, labelKey "category", valueKey "amount", unit $state /result/currency

regions.title: Good to know
regions.purpose: Practical notes for getting around and staying comfortable, kept under the budget in the rail so they don't interrupt the days.
elements: Section with small number "03", title "Good to know"
Vertical Stack repeated over /result/practical_notes: Text value $item (one note per line, small gap between)

brief:
# Result page: trip_planner.plan_trip

Plan the trip day by day, within the budget

## Frame

This page is the result page of an app that is composed, then shows its result: what the person sees after one run. The host draws what surrounds it: the band with the team's logo and the app's name, then a bar restating the request with a way back to edit it and to run again. The host also owns the actions on the result, such as downloading or sharing it, and places them where the page's header puts them. There is no side panel, no app bar and no footer to build, and nothing restates the request.

The page is the result across the full width. It opens on its header, which names the result in a person's words, read from the result itself where it can be (the page's h1). Then the figure or the fact a person looks for first, then the body of the result in the shape it naturally has: a plan day by day, options side by side to compare, a record's details. Lay out what a person reads; leave out what only a machine would.

## State

The host loads the run's result under `/result` before the page renders. Read every value with `$state`; emit no `/state` patches. Paths:

- `/result` — structure trip_planner.Itinerary: A day-by-day plan for a trip, with its estimated cost
  - `/result/title` — text — `title`: The trip's name
  - `/result/overview` — text — `overview`: The plan in two or three sentences
  - `/result/days` — list of structure trip_planner.DayPlan — `days`: The plan for each day, in order
    - each item is a structure trip_planner.DayPlan (One day of the trip), with these members (paths relative to one item, for DataTable columns or $item):
      - `day` — date — `day`: The day
      - `title` — text — `title`: What the day is about, in a few words
      - `morning` — text — `morning`: What to do in the morning
      - `midday` — text — `midday`: Where and what to eat at midday
      - `afternoon` — text — `afternoon`: What to do in the afternoon
      - `evening` — text — `evening`: What to do in the evening
  - `/result/costs` — list of structure trip_planner.CostLine — `costs`: The estimated cost, by category
    - each item is a structure trip_planner.CostLine (One line of the estimated cost), with these members (paths relative to one item, for DataTable columns or $item):
      - `category` — choice of "stay" | "food" | "tickets" | "transport" | "buffer" — `category`: What the money goes on
      - `amount` — number — `amount`: The estimated amount, in the trip's currency
  - `/result/estimated_total` — number — `estimated_total`: The estimated total cost of the trip
  - `/result/currency` — text — `currency`: The currency of every amount
  - `/result/practical_notes` — list of text — `practical_notes`: Notes for getting around and staying comfortable
    - each item is a text

## Delegated

None. `MthdsResult` remains available for any structure you choose not to lay out.

## One real run, as loaded

The state of one actual run, so you can judge magnitudes and lengths. Bind to the paths; do not copy these values into the spec.
